items.followUp: How many significant figures are in (i) 450.0 and (ii) 0.0062?

rubric.why: The trailing zeros after the decimal point are significant.
rubric.description: Correct number of significant figures in 275.00.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for five significant figures.

rubric.why: Leading zeros are not significant; the digits 2 and 7 count.
rubric.description: Correct number of significant figures in 0.027.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two significant figures.

items.followUp: Define derived units and give the SI base units of length and mass.

rubric.why: Base units are independent units and are not defined in terms of other units.
rubric.description: Defines base units as independent units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base units are independent or are not derived from other units.

rubric.why: The SI base unit of temperature is kelvin (K), and that of electric current is ampere (A).
rubric.description: Gives both required SI base units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both units; do not award this mark for only one correct unit.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent units that are not defined in terms of other units.
The base unit of temperature is kelvin (K).
The base unit of electric current is ampere (A).

items.followUp: Differentiate between translatory motion and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: In circular motion, an object moves along a circular path around a point outside the object.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object moves along a circular path around an external point or centre.

rubric.why: In rotatory motion, a body spins about an axis passing through it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body rotates or spins about an axis through itself.

modelAnswer: In circular motion, an object moves along a circular path around a point outside the object.
In rotatory motion, a body spins about an axis passing through the body.

rubric.why: Newton's second law relates force to mass and acceleration: F = ma.
rubric.description: Connects force to the acceleration of a mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a force acts on a mass of 1 kg.

rubric.why: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².
rubric.description: States the defining acceleration for one newton.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the acceleration produced is 1 m/s².

modelAnswer: One newton is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg.

items.followUp: What is the difference between concurrent and non-concurrent forces?

rubric.why: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that like parallel forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: Define the centre of gravity of a body.

rubric.why: A rigid body does not change its shape or size, so the distance between its particles remains fixed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that distances between points or particles of the body remain constant.

rubric.why: The line of action is the straight line along which the force acts.
rubric.description: Defines the line of action of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the line along which the force acts.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is one in which the distance between any two points remains constant.
The line of action of a force is the straight line along which the force acts.

items.followUp: Why do we feel the gravitational pull of Earth but not the pull between two nearby objects?

rubric.why: The masses of ordinary objects are small, so their mutual gravitational attraction is very small.
rubric.description: Identifies the small masses of everyday objects as the reason.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ordinary objects have small masses.

rubric.why: Their gravitational force is too small to produce a perceptible effect.
rubric.description: Explains why the force cannot be felt.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resulting gravitational attraction is too weak or too small to feel.

modelAnswer: The masses of ordinary objects around us are small.
Therefore, the gravitational force between them is very small and cannot be felt.

items.followUp: A force of 10 N moves a body 3 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.

rubric.why: Work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force.
rubric.description: Defines work in terms of force and displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that work is done when a force produces displacement in its direction.

rubric.why: Work depends on the magnitude of the force and the displacement in the force's direction.
rubric.description: Identifies the factors on which work depends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both force and displacement.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force produces displacement in the direction of the force.
Work depends on the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
